analysis:
Only test code changed in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift: the head patch adds two tests at lines 807-839. They cover scoped stop-string matching (EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope for gpt-oss) and EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request carrying stopStringScope into CBv2Request. The supplied units do not include the production implementation. I only saw the patch excerpt for those new tests, not the head text around lines 807-839. I could not verify the production behavior of stopStringScope or matchedStopSequence. Nothing in the visible test diff alters trust boundaries, authorization, attestation, encryption, or key handling.

The rest of the supplied head text (lines 1-676) and the base text (2469-3127) are context for the same file. The tests exercise prefix-cache behavior under T-041. That includes SSD receipt/callback isolation across scopes, cacheSalt mapping, and the pump-receipt lifecycle. They assert existing protections: scope-isolated callbacks, no donation on a demand hint of 0, receipt cleanup on cancel, and zero staged bytes afterwards. These tests reinforce rather than weaken the T-041 mitigations. The test fixtures use temp directories and in-test symmetric keys, with no secrets.

Remaining question for integration: confirm that the stop-string scoping production change, which is outside these units, does not let consumer-supplied stop strings match inside hidden analysis-channel text. Stop sequences are consumer-controlled, and output-truncation semantics rather than confidentiality are affected. No finding on the supplied evidence.
